business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Speed Dipping Production of Powder-Free Synthetic Nitrile Gloves

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 41 de 2007 (as amended by Ley 23 de 2015 and Ley 70 de 2019) on combating money laundering and terrorist financing; Decreto de Gabinete No. 2 de 2015; Executive Decree No. 363 de 2021 on AML/CFT compliance; Unique Client Registry (Registro Único de Clientes) regulations issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF); Law 21 of 2017 creating the UAF and Directorio; Registry of Beneficial Owners under Executive Decree No. 129 of 2020 implementing Law 52 of 2016 on the register of final beneficial owners of legal vehicles; Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público) resolution governing disclosure of legal persons' beneficial ownership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation of Foundation Charter and internal regulations into Spanish
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified public translator authorized by the Supreme Court of Justice of Panama (Corte Suprema de Justicia)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of translator's signature where translation originates abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of No Tax Debt / Solvency Certificate (Visto Bueno or Paz y Salvo)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal verification; no foreign apostille required if issued in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Persona Jurídica)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Legal Representation Appointment and Notarized Corporate Resolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public and Public Registry of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies, banking reference letters, and professional references of initial beneficiaries and proposed directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing authority in country of origin; notarization by local notary; embassies/consulates
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for countries not party to Hague Apostille; otherwise Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all founders, foundation council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Panama's national public interest list (Listado de Personas, empresas y organizaciones vinculadas al terrorismo) published by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP (Politically Exposed Person) identified under FATF Recommendations 12 and 22, including foreign, domestic, and international organization PEPs; must verify source of wealth and source of funds to the satisfaction of the compliance officer of the resident agent (agente residente) under Law 21 of 2017 and UAF regulations. Ongoing transaction monitoring must include screening against Interpol alerts and World Bank debarment lists where relevant to medical procurement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Registro de Personas Jurídicas / Sistema de Consulta de Nombres) online trademark and corporate name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Name must be in Spanish or any language using Latin characters; if proposed in non-Latin script, a Spanish transliteration must be submitted. Spanish language version prevails for registration. Foundation names may include 'Fundación' or 'Private Interest Foundation' and must be distinct from all existing corporate, foundation, and trademark names. The name may not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity, and cannot include a name that suggests government affiliation, public bodies, or regulated professions unless authorized.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerial approval required: 'Seguro Social', 'Municipio', 'Comunidad', 'Ministerio de Salud', 'MINSA', 'CSS', 'Servicio'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration/review petition (recurso de reconsideración apelación) within 5 business days of notification of rejection, attaching a first (primera) alternate name and a second (segunda) alternate name. The petition must be filed by the registered agent with a sworn statement that the alternate names are not misleading. If the registry denies the appeal, a new name clearance request must be filed; the filing fee is non-refundable but a discounted fee applies for immediate resubmission of approved alternate names. In case of substantive constitutional or procedural harm, annulment action (demanda contencioso-administrativa) may be brought before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within 2 months of final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as a statutory registered office for a Private Interest Foundation. Under Law 25 of 1995 (as amended by Law 19 of 2001), every foundation must have a resident agent (agente residente) in Panama with a physical street address. The resident agent's office may serve as the registered office and is the designated address for legal service of process. A virtual office may be used only for operational correspondence and marketing, not as the legal registered office. For manufacturing of sterile nitrile examination gloves under ISIC 3250, local business permits require physical production facilities; the registered office address cannot be a mere virtual office or P.O. box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to High (60-75%): Medical device and PPE manufacturing is regulated by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) and STRI/Intendencia de Supervisión y Regulación; MINSA may conduct unannounced inspections of manufacturing facilities for Good Manufacturing Practices compliance; the local registered office may also be subject to inspection by the Public Registry and municipal tax authorities upon complaint or routine audit. Risk elevated if claiming local substance without actual premises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation name clearance and reservation fee (two alternate names checked)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Executive Decree No. 56 of 2016 (Public Registry Fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foundation charter drafting and notarization (professional legal fee inclusive of statutory notary fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm / Notario Público
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Private Interest Foundation formation (USD 800-1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration fee for Private Interest Foundation at Public Registry of Panama
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff applied on sliding scale; estimate for initial capital of USD 10,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent service fee for first year under Law 25 of 1995
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent (abogado), registered with Registro Público

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Issuance of foundation certificates and apostilled certified copies (registered by-laws, legal representative certification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / Ministerio de Gobierno (Apostille Office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per document plus Apostille fee (USD 10 per document; certified copies USD 10-25)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Acquisition of Tax Identification Number (RUC – Registro Único de Contribuyente) and DGI taxpayer registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee zero; professional handling fee and compliance cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual municipal operating license / Aviso de Operación (pre-incorporation provisional economic activity permit for future plant)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipio de Panamá (or municipal district where registered office/plant will sit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal tariff based on stated gross revenue (minimum tier)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) establishment pre-application for medical device manufacturing (sanitary license pre-clearance for sterile glove manufacturing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Salud, Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas / Dispositivos Médicos
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Executive Decree No. 31 of 2020 (sanitary registration and vigilance fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO filing fee and beneficial ownership register compliance (initial filing with UAF or Public Registry electronic system)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) / Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government filing fee plus professional compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP/sanctions screening database queries (WorldCheck PII/Refinitiv or Thomson Reuters; three-tier screening for initial identities)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance technology provider / external AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per profile screening (USD 15-30 per individual or double-check via OFAC/UN free lists)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign company documents and corporate records (IF ANY: mother company, director passports, utility bills)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified public translator authorized by Corte Suprema de Justicia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Consular section of origin country embassy in Panama / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff per document (USD 40-150 per document depending on source country)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Régimen Jurídico de las Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley No. 5 de 6 de abril de 2015; Articles 6-9 (constitution and registration), 13 (use of foreign languages), 17 (organs), 24-27 (Foundation Council and Protector), and 31 (winding-up); together with the General Regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) – Dirección General; Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Archivo e Inscripción.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de la Fundación de Interés Privado (Public Foundation Deed) – submitted as the original first Testimonio issued by the Notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama Law No. 25 of 1995 prescribes no statutory minimum paid-up capital; the founder must, however, make a real and identifiable transfer of assets to the Foundation's patrimony. Prevailing banking and AML practice requires a minimum initial endowment of US$10,000 evidenced by bank documentation. No escrow or blocked account is statutorily mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [NAME] FOUNDATION — ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY AT THE ORGANIZATIONAL MEETING ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the Founder has evidenced the initial endowment and appointed the undersigned Foundation Council members, THE COUNCIL RESOLVES: 1. To accept the founder's subscription of the initial endowment and formally constitute the Foundation's capital. 2. To adopt the registered office: Calle [__], Edificio [__], Corregimiento de [__], Panama City, Republic of Panama, as the legal domicile. 3. To appoint [Name] President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Protector of the Foundation Council for five-year terms, with joint authority. 4. To authorize the registered agent to execute Public Registry filings and open corporate bank accounts. APPROVED this ___ day of ____, 20__.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-registration Name Verification and Reservation (Certificado de Registro de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, via Sede Electrónica or counter windows.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Foundation name with one alternative and pay the name search tariff. The RPP verifies the absence of identical or confusingly similar registered names and issues a Certificado de Registro de Nombre valid for the statutory reservation term. The certificate must be attached to the foundation deed executed in Step 2.
required_dossiers: RPP name search application form
Payment receipt of the search tariff
Simple copy of the founder's identification document
Proposed name and one alternative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or contested by an existing registrant, submit a new search using the alternative name, or obtain a written consent waiver from the earlier name holder; amend the draft charter before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la Provincia de Panamá (Panama City Notary Public).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A Panamanian attorney drafts the bilingual Spanish/English Foundation charter and by-laws (normas de gobierno). The founder(s) appear before the Notary, declare the endowment and initial governance structure, and sign together with two attesting witnesses. The Notary keeps the deed in the protocol and issues the original testimonio (first registered copy) and notarial copies.
required_dossiers: RPP name certificate (Step 1)
Bilingual draft of foundation charter and by-laws
Certified passport or cédula copies of the founder(s)
List of the initial Foundation Council members and Protector
Bank reference or asset assignment letter evidencing the initial endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary detects inconsistencies, prepare a corrected re-executed deed or a separate clarification deed (aclaración) to cure variances before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Public Registry Tariffs and Panamanian Stamp Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá and authorized collection agents; Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) tariffs; Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for stamp tax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the RPP registration tariff based on the declared capital and page count of the deed; deposit the tariff via government collection codes or a cashier's check, and retain the stamped collection receipt together with the stamp tax (pólvora) receipt which must be presented with the filing.
required_dossiers: Original testimonio of the foundation deed
RPP tariff schedule and fee computation sheet
Bank payment receipt of tariff and stamp tax
Copy of the name certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tariff is under-computed, pay the differential plus any surcharge and obtain a revised receipt; never file with an incomplete tax stamp to avoid preventive notes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Legal Review of the Foundation Deed with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the stamped testimonio and accompanying dossiers at the RPP entrance (Diario). The RPP assigns an accession number and a registry attorney reviews legality, page count, tariff and compliance with Ley No. 25. The file remains subject to preventive notes (notas de defectos) until inscription.
required_dossiers: Stamped original testimonio of the Escritura Pública
RPP name certificate
Payment receipts for tariff and stamp tax
Official contact address or Apartado Postal in Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer any preventive note within the statutory five-business-day term by filing explanatory or supplementary documents, or a clarification deed; rectify and re-file within the granted extension, and appeal a rejection to the Registry Director (Recurso de Apelación).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Edict Posting, Oppositions and Third-Party Claim Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) – Public Edict and Notices Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RPP publicly posts an edict containing the foundation's corporate data, including name, date, notary and endowment, on the registry's official billboard and electronic portal. The law opens a short legal term for judicial or third-party oppositions based on proprietary or naming claims.
required_dossiers: Registered copy of the filed deed
Edict text prepared by the RPP Office
Proof of edict posting (certification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an opposition or caveat is lodged, the applicant may withdraw and reform the deed, negotiate a settlement or consent, or defend the claim before the civil courts; after resolution, the applicant renews the registration request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificado de Fundación and Registered Testimonios
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the edict term closes and legal review is satisfied, the RPP inscribes the foundation and issues the Certificado de Fundación (registration certificate) evidencing the Foundation's legal personality, together with a registered copy of the by-laws and registered testimonios.
required_dossiers: Favorable registry review resolution
Final by-laws text for stamping and certification
Claim form for certified copies and certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For registry errors, file a reposición petition to correct the entry; for a lost certificate, request an issued duplicate second testimonio under the RPP certification procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Employer Enrollment under the Territorial Regime
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Formulario RUC-001 via the DGI Sede Electrónica or collection desks to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes number for the Foundation as a Panamanian-source taxpayer and employer. Thereafter register as an employer with CSS (Patrono No.) and with MITRADEL for labor and occupational health obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Fundación and registered testimonio
Notarized appointment of legal representative and Council resolution
Formulario RUC 001 (original and copy)
Proof of local registered office address
CSS employer registration form and payroll plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects or queries the RUC application, correct the data and re-submit digitally or before the Ventanilla de Atención al Contribuyente; if the representative appointment is challenged, present the notarized registered copy of the Foundation resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Activation of the Industrial Licensing Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias y Tecnología; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Dispositivos Médicos.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the municipal application and pay the patent tax to obtain the Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Permit). In parallel, file with MICI the Registro de Operación Industrial (industrial start-up notification) and open the MINSA sanitary registration dossier for the sterile nitrile examination glove product line, scheduling the mandatory pre-inspection of the dipping facility and GMP audit.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certificado de Fundación
Notarized Council resolution appointing the plant supervisor
Municipal patent and aviso application and tax receipt
MINSA technical file: device description, sterilization validation, ISO 13485 certificate, biocompatibility and permeability test reports, and labeling
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For municipal objections, correct the classification and tariff of the patent tax; for MICI or MINSA observations, respond within the granted 30-day cure period, complete missing technical submissions, and re-schedule the GMP inspection through the Single Window for Investment (Ventanilla Única).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias y Tecnología (industrial operations); Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Dispositivos Médicos (medical device sanitary registration); Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (environmental permitting).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro y Permiso de Operación Industrial (Industrial Operating Permit) under Ley No. 6 de 1986 and its regulatory Decrees, together with the Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos (Sanitary Registration) for powder-free sterile examination nitrile gloves issued by MINSA.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría II – Estudio de Impacto Ambiental (moderate-impact EIA report) per Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009, applicable to chemical dipping and latex/nitrile glove manufacturing lines; an annual Reporte de Cumplimiento Ambiental (RCA) is required after approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater discharges must comply with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 37 de 1999 (MiAMBIENTE): pH 6.0–9.0; BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L; COD ≤ 200 mg/L; TSS ≤ 100 mg/L; oil and grease ≤ 20 mg/L; total cyanide ≤ 0.5 mg/L; phenols ≤ 0.5 mg/L; temperature increase ≤ 5 °C. Air emissions: nitrile/solvent fugitive VOC controls, stack VOC limit ≤ 100 mg/m³ as carbon, and scrubber or carbon adsorption where required; odor and particulate compliance is verified by periodic MiAMBIENTE inspection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; structural and electrical installation inspection certificates from the municipal Engineering Office (Inspección de Estructuras and Instalaciones Eléctricas); occupational health approval from MITRADEL – Dirección de Inspección y Salud Ocupacional and CSS employer registration; mandatory medical surveillance program for glove factory workers exposed to nitrile polymers, coagulants and volatile solvents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; electronic portal 'Sede Electrónica' at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Execute the Private Interest Foundation charter before a Panamanian Notary and file it with the Public Registry. The PIF must appoint a Panamanian resident agent (abogado idóneo). Submit the RUC registration application to DGI through the Sede Electrónica, attaching the registered foundation charter, resident agent acceptance, fiscal address evidence, foundation council identification, and any banking license/operating authorization. DGI performs a physical inspection, issues the provisional RUC, and then the definitive RUC. For VAT purposes, the taxpayer must simultaneously register for ITBMS and obtain DGI digital signature certificates for electronic invoicing. The foreign parent/founder need not appear physically if represented by the resident agent under a notarized power of attorney.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not have a check-the-box election. The PIF is a separate juridical person and is taxed at entity level only on Panama-source income; foreign-source income is outside the scope of the Income Tax Code. For ITBMS, a taxpayer with annual gross receipts not exceeding PAB 36,000 may elect the simplified small-taxpayer regime, but a manufacturer-exporter of sterile gloves should elect the general regime in order to claim input VAT credits and zero-rate exports. No hybrid mismatch elections are available as Panama has not enacted domestic OECD BEPS Action 2 rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios; VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 0 - no general registration threshold; simplified small-taxpayer regime only for annual gross receipts not exceeding PAB 36,000
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory DGI-authorized electronic invoicing for all registered taxpayers. Invoices must be transmitted in real time through DGI's Facturación Electrónica system using a digital signature, QR code, and DGI fiscal authorization code. Export invoices must clearly indicate the zero-rated cause and reference the customs export declaration. No paper invoices are permitted unless DGI has granted a specific temporary authorization.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to export sales of goods by the PIF-manufacturer when the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory under an approved export declaration and title passes to a foreign buyer. The exporter must be the legal seller and consignor on the shipping documents. Input ITBMS incurred on the production of zero-rated exports may be credited and refunded. Services used abroad are zero-rated only when the recipient is foreign and the benefit is realized abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (B/L or HAWB)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama imposes no exchange-control repatriation deadline. DGI may audit zero-rated exports within a five-year statute of limitations, extended to ten years in cases of fraud. If the mandatory export documentation bundle is incomplete or false, DGI will claw back the uncollected ITBMS plus monthly interest, impose fines up to 100% of the omitted tax, and refer criminal tax fraud cases which may result in imprisonment of four to six years. Exporters must retain the full documentation bundle for at least five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank; the banking regulator is the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de la República de Panamá), and the U.S. dollar is legal tender, with the Panamanian balboa serving only as a nominal fractional unit pegged 1:1.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system with no exchange controls. Current and capital account transactions, including profit remittances, dividends, foundation distributions, and capital repatriation, are freely convertible and transferable in U.S. dollars. The absence of a domestic central monetary authority removes the contractual convertibility risk present in managed-float regimes, though AML/CFT compliance remains the primary operational gate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in Panama. Exporters, manufacturers, and trading entities may retain, allocate, and disburse export receipts in U.S. dollars without mandatory conversion timelines or forced sale ratios. The only applicable obligations are those imposed by banks for transaction records, economic substance documentation, and tax disclosure under Panama's territorial taxation regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital EMI/fintech providers without a Panamanian banking license have Low-to-Medium viability as primary treasury rails. The Superintendency of Banks does not recognize offshore electronic money institutions as licensed banks for deposits, and such institutions normally cannot open clearing accounts in Panama or participate in local ACH. The PIF should rely on Panama-licensed banks for all settlement; offshore EMIs may be used only for contract tracking and secondary payment orchestration with strict client money segregation and sanctions compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted in Panama for private interest foundations if the foundation's incorporating notary, legal counsel, and directors are fully identified. A physical appearance of directors is not statutorily mandated; however, the onboarding bank may require either (a) a physical visit to a Panamanian branch if the natural person director appears on the foundation deed, or (b) an authenticated remote interview via bank-approved video call complemented by notarized and apostilled corporate documents. The accepted practice is a hybrid KYC: remote document review plus mandatory video identification of signatories and ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Founding settlor and beneficiary identity obscured by the private foundation's inherent confidentiality provisions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incumbency issued by the registered foundation; apostilled copy of the foundation charter; internal sworn declaration of the natural-person beneficial owner; and a legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney confirming that the PIF is Law 25-compliant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital injection is not supported by bankable documentary evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of source-bank statements, signed sales or purchase contracts, audited financial statements if the contributor is an entity, personal tax returns or proof of wealth generation, and a notarized source-of-wealth affidavit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose of the account is inconsistent with the foundation's registered object, suggesting financial shell or concealment behavior
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation purpose clause and business plan referencing the production and export of nitrile examination gloves under ISIC 3250; a full corporate organizational chart showing the PIF's ownership of the Panama operating company; and a functional cost/revenue model showing the account as treasury conduit for real trade flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure through downstream counterparties subject to sanctions or PEP (Politically Exposed Person) screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SALES CONTRACT WITH STERILIZATION CERTIFICATIONS, governmental or hospital procurement purchase orders, updated Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) scanning reports, and prophylactic wraparound KYC files for the production factory, along with the PIF's written commitment to decline sanctioned medical institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wire transfers should be sent in U.S. dollars via SWIFT MT103 from the original contributor's regulated bank account to the PIF's Panama operational or escrow account. The SWIFT field 70 remittance information must clearly state the capital contribution, e.g., /INVP/FOUNDATION CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION, and reference the foundation name. The originating bank should apply Customer Due Diligence before sending; the receiving Panamanian bank will rely on its own AML file. For shareholder loans, a formal loan agreement and interest schedule should be retained. Verification is completed by matching the contributor's legal name against the foundation's register of contributors and confirming the transaction orchestration against the PIF's treasury approval matrix.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of medical glove sales and raw material purchases will be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and MT700 for irrevocable documentary letters of credit. For high-value export transactions, the buyer's bank can open an LC with the Panamanian bank presented as the confirming or advising bank. Inbound export proceeds are collected through the Panamanian bank's correspondents on Fedwire or CHIPS for U.S.-dollar checks and remittances. Factory disbursements to latex or nitrile polymer suppliers in ASEAN jurisdictions will use direct MT103 payments or MT700 commercial letters of credit, always with Incoterms 2020 specifications and export cargo insurance documentation attached to the trade file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright U.S. Dollar forwards against Euro and Renminbi receivable positions
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on Latin American and ASEAN soft currencies where physical delivery is restricted
Cross-currency swaps matching USD receipts to EUR or CNY purchase obligations
Plain-vanilla FX options for hedging the PIF's net commodity-cost exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of the annual franchise tax (Tasa Única Anual) applicable to a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995, as amended by Law 8 of 2010
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; remitted by the registered agent on behalf of the foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar fiscal year; fee is payable within the first quarter, with final deadline on March 31 of each year. Registered agents commonly require client funding by January 31 to guarantee timely DGI settlement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% statutory surcharge plus default interest on the unpaid annual fee. Persistent non-payment for successive years, together with the resident agent's resignation, may lead the Public Registry to cancel the foundation's registration (administrative strike-off) and extinguish its separate legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and ratification of beneficial ownership data in the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, RBF) under Law 70 of 2021, including updates for any change of founders, council members, protectors, or ultimate beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) digital portal, coordinated by the resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the RBF ratification window published by the DGI, typically aligned with the foundation's RBF registration anniversary or the first-quarter portal reopening; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 30 calendar days of the relevant transaction or resolution.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file, update, or annually ratify truthful beneficial ownership information constitutes an administrative infraction under Law 70 of 2021, punishable by fines in the range of USD 500 to USD 2,500; ongoing non-compliance can suspend issuance of good-standing certificates and trigger registry sanctions against the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating and lodgment of foundation accounting records with the resident agent, satisfying the record-keeping duty under Law 25 of 1995 and the AML/CFT obligations of Law 23 of 2015
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulator; records must be physically available at the foundation's registered office or with the resident agent and producible on demand to the AML supervisory authorities of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of the foundation's inscription in the Public Registry; records must reflect all foundation transactions and the financial position as of the prior December 31 fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current accounting records breaches Law 25 of 1995 and Law 23 of 2015; the resident agent may resign after notice if records are not supplied, and the foundation may face registry cancellation, loss of legal personality, and inability to continue its banking and trade operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is imposed on a Panama Private Interest Foundation solely under Law 25 of 1995. Mandatory audit obligations arise only if the foundation becomes a DGI-registered local taxpayer conducting Panama-source commercial activity, if consolidated fiscal attestation thresholds under the Código Fiscal are met, or if the foundation is supervised as a financial entity. A foundation directly operating the nitrile-glove dipping plant would be treated as a commercial taxpayer and must keep auditable books; in addition, banks, medical licensors, and tender counterparties typically require externally audited statements as a contractual condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama applies to public-interest and larger entities; IFRS for SMEs or Panamanian local GAAP (NIF) may be applied by private entities not listed on the securities market. Where the foundation is a DGI-registered operator, books must be maintained in Spanish, supported by vouchers, and subject to the retention and formalization rules of the Código Fiscal.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must identify, verify, and retain current records of the foundation's founders, council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficial owners from incorporation onward under Law 23 of 2015. Under Law 70 of 2021, the foundation must also file and annually ratify beneficiary-ownership data in the DGI-operated RBF. Any transfer of the economic interest in the foundation — whether by amendment of the foundation charter, substitution of the founder, assignment of beneficial entitlement, or change of control over the Foundation Council — must be documented by a notarially certified resolution, reflected in the foundation's records, and updated in the RBF within 30 days of the change. The annual confirmation is performed by the resident agent jointly with the Foundation Council by verifying and ratifying the existing RBF record, or by filing an updated declaration when a material change has occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation charter (acta de constitución) and regulations, including all amendments registered in the Public Registry
Foundation Council minute book and corporate resolutions ledger
Register of beneficiaries, foundation council members, and protectors, with complete UBO identification data
Accounting records and supporting vouchers covering all foundation assets, liabilities, income, and expenditures
AML/CFT client file maintained by the resident agent, including customer due diligence, risk assessment, and source-of-funds documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – 800 per annum for resident agent and registered office services, inclusive or exclusive of the USD 350 government annual fee depending on the service agreement; higher fees apply where the foundation holds operating subsidiaries or complex UBO structures requiring enhanced compliance work
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – 4,500 for a certified public accountant review of foundation statutory and accounting records; full IFRS audited financial statements for a manufacturing operating entity typically range from USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 and are not a statutory requirement for the foundation itself

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% ISR on net Panamanian-source income; a Private Interest Foundation without Panamanian-source commercial activity is not a CIT taxpayer and bears only the US$300 annual franchise fee.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial regime: foreign-source manufacturing and trading profits (including export sales of sterile nitrile gloves) are outside Panama's tax base, yielding a 0% effective rate for a compliant non-resident PIF; Panamanian-source income is taxable at 25% after deductions; export/SEM and treaty structures can reduce local burdens; no gross-assets tax applies to PIFs.
